tasks.gr10-self-awareness-self-esteem-t1: Topic: Self-awareness, Self-esteem and Self-development. Cover knowing your own strengths, weaknesses, feelings and values, how family, friends, results, culture and the media shape self-esteem, strategies for building confidence in yourself and others (communicating, completing tasks, taking part in community life, making good decisions, affirming others), and respecting the uniqueness of self and others (race, gender, ability). Ask Grade 10 learners to explain the difference between self-awareness and self-esteem, analyse the effect of media images, choose strategies to build confidence, or respond respectfully to a difference in a scenario.
tasks.gr10-power-gender-t1: Topic: Power, Power Relations and Gender. Cover the meaning of power and power relations and the difference between using and abusing power, the difference between sex and gender, masculinity, femininity, gender roles and stereotypes (including in sport), and how gender inequality affects relationships and wellbeing (sexual abuse, violence, teenage pregnancy, STIs including HIV and AIDS). Ask Grade 10 learners to classify a statement as biological or a gender role, identify a stereotype and a fair response, or analyse pressure in a relationship and say where help is available. Keep every item age-appropriate, factual and free of graphic detail.
tasks.gr10-subjects-career-fields-t1: Topic: Subjects, Career Fields and Study Choices. Cover interests, abilities, talents and strengths, the difference between a career field, an occupation, a job and a career, the National Senior Certificate subject requirements (two languages, Mathematics or Mathematical Literacy, Life Orientation and three other subjects), the steps in making a career decision, the life domains of being, becoming and community, and socio-economic factors including the effect of income tax on net salary. Ask Grade 10 learners to match terms to examples, order decision steps, choose subjects for a career goal, or work out net pay from gross pay and deductions.
tasks.gr10-diversity-discrimination-t1: Topic: Diversity, Discrimination and Human Rights Violations. Cover the meaning of diversity, discrimination and human rights violations in contexts such as race, religion, culture, language, gender, age, rural or urban living, xenophobia, human trafficking and HIV and AIDS status, the difference between bias, prejudice and discrimination, the impact of discrimination on individuals and society, and how individuals and organisations challenge prejudice. Ask Grade 10 learners to name the type of discrimination in a scenario, explain prejudice versus discrimination, or choose a responsible way to challenge unfair treatment.
tasks.gr10-bill-of-rights-instruments-t1: Topic: The Bill of Rights and International Instruments. Cover the Bill of Rights in Chapter 2 of the Constitution (1996), rights with responsibilities, the limitation of rights, the Convention on the Rights of the Child (United Nations, 1989), the African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child (1990), CEDAW (United Nations, 1979), protection bodies such as the South African Human Rights Commission, the Commission for Gender Equality, the Public Protector, Legal Aid South Africa and the courts, school codes of conduct, and campaigns such as Human Rights Day and the 16 Days of Activism. Ask Grade 10 learners to match a right or a situation to the right instrument or body, explain why a right can be limited, or choose the first step to take when a right is violated.
tasks.gr10-physical-education-t1: Topic: Physical Education: Fitness and Safety. Cover cardiovascular fitness, muscular strength, muscular endurance and flexibility, the value of regular exercise programmes for physical and mental health, the World Health Organization advice of an average of at least 60 minutes of activity a day for children and teenagers, the warm-up, main activity and cool-down, and safety in fitness exercises. Ask Grade 10 learners to match an activity to a fitness component, explain how exercise helps mental health, add up the minutes in a session or a week, or choose the safe response to pain or dizziness.
